title: Compact invocation lattice and materialized views for Console aggregates
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Create a compact, join-minimizing invocation lattice and a set of materialized views to serve the most common Console analytics slices (cost attribution, latency by route, tenant adoption trends) with sub-second to low-second query latency for tenant-scoped queries. This ticket covers the schema design, ETL transforms from raw callstream, a write-efficient materialization strategy, and a backwards-compatible migration path from current sessionized aggregates. The lattice approach groups events into a small set of denormalized fact shapes that can be incrementally updated and used to derive both wide per-tenant aggregates and fine-grained debugging tables without repeated heavy joins.
acceptance_criteria: Design documented with expected table sizes, partitioning, and index strategy
Implement base ingestion transform that produces the compact invocation lattice from raw callstream within existing Spark pipeline
Create three materialized views: tenant_daily_facts, route_latency_histograms, and tenant_model_variant_usage that refresh incrementally and are queryable from console BI dashboards
End-to-end tests validating data parity against current denormalized source for a 30-day sample (within 0.5% for aggregate counts)
Query performance: tenant_scoped median query < 400ms p50 and p95 < 1200ms for common filters (tenant_id + date range)
Rollback plan and migration checklist documented
tech_notes: Core idea: map raw invocation events to a compact key (tenant_id, route_id, invocation_window_id, model_variant_hash) and emit a single lattice row that contains counts, sum_tokens, latency_quantile_buckets (pre-aggregated histogram), first_seen_ts, last_seen_ts, and JSON metadata for edge-case debugging
Storage: Parquet tables partitioned by tenant_id (high cardinality) + date_hour for faster tenant-scoped scans. Consider synthetic tenant shards for very small tenants to reduce partition explosion.
Indexing: Use a sparse secondary index on route_id+model_variant_hash for cross-tenant route analytics. Where DB supports it, use min-max column stats and Bloom filters for large string fields.
Materialized views refresh: incremental by watermark; source pipeline will emit change batches (upserts) and a lightweight merge job will apply to materialized views hourly
Back-compat: expose old view names as read-only aliases to the new materialized views so dashboards and SQL endpoints don't need immediate rewrites
Cost considerations: materialized views will increase storage by ~15-25% depending on compression but should reduce total query compute by >40% for BI workloads
KV-cache and concurrency: design writes to avoid large per-tenant hotspots by batching commits and using idempotent merge keys
migration_plan: Phase 1: Design review and perf modeling using a 90-day sample of callstream; validate expected cardinalities
Phase 2: Implement transform in ETL sandbox and run daily job to produce lattice table alongside existing pipeline for N days
Phase 3: Create incremental materialized view refresh jobs and run in read-only mode for comparison; generate data parity reports
Phase 4: Flip dashboards and alerting to point at new materialized views for low-risk tenants; monitor latency and correctness
Phase 5: Full cutover and decommission legacy denorm views after 4 weeks of stable parity metrics and SLOs
db_schema: lattice_invocations_v1: tenant_id STRING, route_id STRING, invocation_window_id STRING, model_variant_hash STRING, invocation_count BIGINT, sum_prompt_tokens BIGINT, sum_completion_tokens BIGINT, latency_millis_p50 INT, latency_millis_p95 INT, latency_histogram BINARY (pre-agg), first_seen_ts TIMESTAMP, last_seen_ts TIMESTAMP, debug_meta STRING (JSON), partition_date DATE
queries_examples:
-- tenant daily aggregates
SELECT partition_date, SUM(invocation_count) as invocations, SUM(sum_prompt_tokens+sum_completion_tokens) as total_tokens FROM lattice_invocations_v1 WHERE tenant_id = 't_123' AND partition_date BETWEEN '2025-02-01' AND '2025-02-28' GROUP BY partition_date ORDER BY partition_date;

-- route latency percentiles for tenant slice
SELECT route_id, APPROX_QUANTILES(latency_millis_p50, 100)[OFFSET(50)] as p50_est FROM lattice_invocations_v1 WHERE tenant_id = 't_123' AND partition_date = '2025-03-01' GROUP BY route_id ORDER BY p50_est DESC LIMIT 50;

-- usage by model variant
SELECT model_variant_hash, SUM(invocation_count) as uses FROM lattice_invocations_v1 WHERE partition_date >= '2025-03-01' GROUP BY model_variant_hash ORDER BY uses DESC LIMIT 100;
notes: Watch out for partition skew from a few very large tenants — we may need dedicated tenant shards for top-10 customers.
Consider later extension: expose compact lattice for nearline feature store to enable real-time feature derivation.
If Bloom filters not supported natively in chosen warehouse, emulate with precomputed hashed inclusion tables for large string fields.
